The model supports binary multiplicities, supplied release/deadline critical times, machine kinds and Configuration IP encodings. Lemma 3 and Appendix A.1 transform a schedule into a bounded cycle description: external cycles can contain at most one job, internal cycles between consecutive critical times can be merged by reordering because all involved release/deadline conditions allow it, and the count is at most 4d-3. The compact schedule-output discussion charges logarithmic dependence on the number of copies. Section 3.1.1 and its appendix reconstruction verify constraints and decoding on the same cycle assignment. Later read portions also cover speed and objective variants at their stated hypotheses. We do not import a polynomial-in-variable-d general IP algorithm or precedence support absent from this model.

Evaluation and realization are inverse bijections. For a root z on a cycle of length l, the coordinate at position k is z^(2^k). The equation z^(2^l-1)=1 gives exactly the wraparound relation. Independent cycle assignments are multiplied pointwise; disjoint supports ensure that evaluation recovers each chosen root separately. Fixed-point coordinates equal one, so singleton cycles contribute mu_1={1}. Complex.card_rootsOfUnity counts every nontrivial cycle factor exactly. The cycles belong to the successor permutation itself.

- The protocol is the Young-index (2, 2) sector of Hayashi–Matsumoto's universal concentration. Their index (3, 1) sector yields a three-dimensional maximally entangled state, which LOCC converts into ϕ+ deterministically. By the Schur weights dim V_λ · s_λ(x, y) of the Schmidt weights x and y, this raises the success probability to 3xy(x² + xy + y²) + 2x²y², which is 11/16 at ψ0.
